classification.difficultyReason: Parts a and b are signposted: differentiate, then compute the discriminant of the derivative. The essential demand is in part c. The student must reframe 'never decreasing' as f'(x)≥0 for all x. They must then link this to an upward-opening quadratic that never goes below the x-axis, and so to discriminant ≤0, including the inclusive boundary k=12. This is a linked routine procedure with one conceptual reframing. The discriminant is supplied, and there is no asymptote or domain subtlety. That makes it slightly harder than p13-practice and clearly easier than p17-q14.

classification.difficultyReason: Parts a and b are routine: differentiate 5/x, justify the sign using x^2>0, and evaluate two values. The hardest demand is part c, where the student must see that a negative derivative only compares values within one interval, and that -2 and 1 lie on opposite sides of the asymptote x=0. That is a real interpretation step. It is more scaffolded than p17-q14, because part b has already produced the two values and part c asks a direct yes/no question rather than asking the student to explain an anomaly. It is harder than the routine stationary-point work in p13-practice.
